previous_statement: Define c0_prime:=max{1,c0}. Then c0_prime>=1 and, by the preceding sign derivation, 0<=c0<=c0_prime. For every 0<=epsilon<=epsilon_max^cb, 0<=c0*epsilon<=c0_prime*epsilon. Thus lem-maincb-extended-inclusion-monotone upgrades every replacement extended (c0*epsilon)-inclusion supplied by lem-maincb-error-improvement to an extended (c0_prime*epsilon)-inclusion. The replacement map itself is unchanged, so its bijectivity whenever the input is bijective is unchanged. Renaming c0_prime as c0 proves that the error-improvement witness may be chosen with c0>=1.
new_statement: Retain the original universal constant c0 furnished by lem-maincb-error-improvement; do not replace it by max{1,c0}. Nodes 1.1.1.1 and 1.1.1.2 show that this same full-scope witness satisfies c0>=0. This is sufficient for the remainder of the proof: node 1.1.2 places 1 and c0 separately inside K_3^0, and the root separately assumes W.K3>=max{K_3^0,1,W.L,W.c0_cb*W.L}; no later hypothesis requires c0>=1. The later use of lem-maincb-extended-inclusion-monotone in node 1.2.3 is within that lemma's scope because the root's target A is explicitly finite-dimensional.
